details: US President Donald Trump has reportedly threatened to declare the Strait of Hormuz a "territory of the United States." This statement follows a recent drone attack on a ship in the Strait and Iran's demand for all passing vessels to seek permission from its military. The escalating tensions and rising oil prices stemming from this key global chokepoint are increasing overall geopolitical risk, which tends to reduce demand for risk assets, including cryptocurrencies.
title: Trump Threatens Hormuz Control Amid US-Iran Conflict

details: The White House is reportedly set to host a significant meeting this week that will include President Trump, executives from prominent cryptocurrency firms like Coinbase and Ripple, and top regulators from the CFTC and SEC. This gathering suggests potential progress toward establishing clearer crypto regulations, with the Clarity Act possibly advancing in the Senate soon. Greater regulatory clarity is generally seen as a positive development that could reduce market risks and foster increased institutional investment in cryptocurrency markets over the long term.
title: White House Schedules Major Meeting on Bitcoin & Crypto Regulation

details: The cryptocurrency market is currently experiencing a downturn, with Bitcoin retesting the $62,000 level. This slump is attributed to a combination of factors, including the Bank of Japan's hawkish stance on accelerating interest rate hikes, which impacts global monetary policy and risk appetite. Additionally, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) recently canceled a planned meeting on crypto regulation, and weak institutional demand, reflected in Bitcoin ETF outflows, are further contributing to reduced investor confidence in the crypto space.
title: Crypto Market Downturn: BoJ Hikes & US Regulatory Stalls Weigh
